text.title: PWA Core Architecture Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules on Service Worker scope and registration, Web App Manifest identity and icons, Workbox strategy-per-route-shape, and the update flow. Each is checkable against sw.js, manifest.json and the registration module; the last rule is the routing/skip leaf.

rule.statement: `sw.js` MUST be served from the origin root (`/sw.js`) with `Cache-Control: no-cache` (or `max-age=0`). Serving it from `/static/`, `/assets/` or any build subdirectory is rejected unless the response also carries `Service-Worker-Allowed: /`.

rationale.source: W3C Service Workers spec — scope + Service-Worker-Allowed header

rule.rationale: Default scope is the path of the script URL, so `/static/sw.js` can only intercept fetches under `/static/`; navigations to `/` are never controlled and the app appears to have no offline support at all. A long-cached `sw.js` is worse: the browser byte-compares the script to decide whether an update exists, so a stale cached copy pins the app to an old precache manifest indefinitely.

rule.statement: The manifest MUST declare an explicit `id` and it MUST NOT change after the first public release. `start_url` may change; `id` may not.
rule.rationale: App identity is the `id` resolved against the manifest URL. With no `id`, identity falls back to `start_url`, so a routing change silently re-keys the app: the browser treats it as a second application, the existing home-screen shortcut keeps pointing at the old identity, and the install prompt reappears for users who already installed.

rule.statement: `icons` MUST include a 192x192 and a 512x512 PNG, and at least one entry with `purpose` containing `maskable`. Shipping every icon as `purpose: "any"` only is rejected.

rationale.source: W3C Web App Manifest `purpose` + Chromium installability criteria

rule.rationale: Android composites the icon inside a platform-chosen mask; an icon drawn edge-to-edge instead of inside the ~80% safe zone gets its logo clipped on the home screen. The 192/512 pair is the installability gate — missing it removes the install prompt entirely with no console error.

rule.statement: Route strategies MUST be assigned by response shape: `NetworkFirst` with `networkTimeoutSeconds: 3` for navigations and `/api/*`; `CacheFirst` + `ExpirationPlugin` for images and fonts; `StaleWhileRevalidate` for content-hashed JS/CSS. Authenticated HTML and per-user API JSON MUST NOT be precached.
rule.rationale: A Cache Storage entry is keyed by request URL and carries no identity, so `CacheFirst` on a personalised response serves the previous user's HTML after logout on a shared device. `NetworkFirst` without a timeout is equivalent to network-only on a captive or transit connection: the request hangs on TCP rather than failing, so the cached fallback is never reached and the user sees a spinner instead of the offline shell.

rule.statement: A waiting worker MUST be surfaced as a user-initiated reload: detect via `registration.addEventListener('updatefound')` → `installing.state === 'installed'` while `navigator.serviceWorker.controller` is non-null, then reload on `controllerchange` after the user accepts. Unconditional `self.skipWaiting()` inside `install` is forbidden.

rationale.source: Service Worker lifecycle / Workbox advanced recipes

rule.rationale: `skipWaiting()` activates the new worker under an already-loaded page. That page then lazy-loads content-hashed chunks belonging to the previous build, which the new precache has just deleted, producing ChunkLoadError mid-session. Reloading without asking additionally discards in-flight form state.

rule.statement: `navigator.serviceWorker.register()` MUST be called exactly once from a bootstrap module (`main.ts` / `index.html`), never inside a React `useEffect`. The deferred `beforeinstallprompt` event MUST be stored at module scope, not in component state of a remountable component.
rule.rationale: StrictMode double-invokes effects in development, producing two registrations and duplicated lifecycle events that make update debugging unreliable. `beforeinstallprompt` fires once per page load, so a component that unmounts before the user clicks Install loses the only reference to it and the install button becomes permanently inert.

rule.statement: Do NOT apply when (a) iOS Safari is the primary target and the requirement depends on Background Sync or offline data surviving more than 7 days — WebKit has no Background Sync API and evicts script-writable storage (IndexedDB, Cache Storage) after 7 days without user interaction; (b) the app is hard real-time (live trading, conferencing) where SW cache coherence adds risk with no offline upside; (c) a native shell (Capacitor, Tauri, React Native) already owns caching and install.

rationale.source: WebKit ITP storage policy + methodology preconditions

rule.rationale: Promising offline behaviour on a platform that evicts the cache produces the worst outcome: the app works in testing, then silently loses the user's queued data after a week of non-use, which is indistinguishable from data loss.
